newsitem.title: USA: Police arrest second bank robbery suspect.
newsitem.headline: Police arrest second bank robbery suspect.

text.p: Police Tuesday arrested a 19-year-old suspect in a brazen bank heist and charged him and his alleged accomplice with killing a bank security guard and bank robbery.

Billie Allen was apprehended at a house several hours after escaping the fiery crash of a van where police found the partially burned cash hoard that he and Norris Holder, 21, were accused of stealing Monday from Lindell Bank & Trust Co.

The two were armed with AK-47 rifles and wore bullet-proof vests and leg armour, which the FBI said was reminiscent of the two assailants in a Hollywood, Calif., bank robbery two weeks ago in which the gunmen fired hundreds of rounds of automatic weapons fire at police before they were killed.
FBI agent Wiley Thompson suggested Monday's robbery may have been a "copy-cat" of the California shootout and said the St. Louis duo "were prepared to die if necessary."
Bank guard Richard Heflin, 46, was shot and killed immediately and the robbers sprayed the lobby with gunfire as two dozen customers dove for cover.
The two then led police on a chase before crashing their van into a tree, where it caught fire.
A flammable accelerant as well as two automatic weapons and an undetermined amount of cash were found in the wrecked van, which police said the robbers had planned to set on fire and abandon.
Holder, who suffered minor burns, was arrested at the scene of the crash while Allen escaped into the wooded park.
